$comment: P69 (lane `cs`, D-LIR-GUARDED-RANGE-DOES-NOT-COVER-BLOCKS-THE-LOWERING-CREATES): A GUARDED REGION IS A SET OF CONTIGUOUS RUNS, ONE SCOPE RECORD PER RUN. An `asm goto` inside a `__try` whose output is a structure the template leaves in a register is stored through the object's address on EACH edge of the statement, in a block the lowering creates for that edge, laid out after every block of the function. The scope table used to hold one byte range per `__try` — the blocks the guarded body's own statements became — so those edge blocks were outside it. MEASURED before (pe64, the mingw-gcc build of DSS, debug AND release, the same in both): `guarded` over a no-access page ended the process with exit code 3221225477 (0xC0000005) instead of 42; in its image the scope was [0x1064, 0x10c8) and the two stores `mov %r9,(%rcx)` sat at 0x10e1 and 0x10ed, the function's last two blocks. For a while the statement was refused by name. Now each maximal run of contiguous created blocks whose owner is a block of the region has a scope record of its own, with the region's filter and handler, after the record of the region's own blocks. Exit bits by return value: 1/2 the unfaulted control (the store is really made on the edge taken), 3 the fault on an edge reaches the handler, 4/5 the same statement two regions deep and unfaulted, 6 the inner filter declines and the fault reaches the OUTER handler (the edge blocks are a run of each region around them). No reference on these hosts compiles both halves (MSVC has no x64 inline asm, mingw gcc no `__try`), so there is no reference exit code to state: 42 is what the program's own text says.
$commentHostCoverage: WHAT EACH HOST ASSERTS OF THIS FILE (the two runners' behaviour as examples/c/declspec_requests_are_honoured_on_pe states it from their sources). On a WINDOWS host both corpus runners compile the pe pair and RUN the image, debug and release: the exit code — that the fault on an edge reaches its handler — is read there and only there. On a host that is NOT Windows the in-process runner (tests/examples) still COMPILES the baseline arm for the pe pair, so a refusal of this statement is caught there, and then stops at `runOn`: it spawns nothing, the exit code is NOT read, and the release arm is not compiled. The CLI-subprocess runner (integrated_tests) binds one host-runnable target per manifest, so off Windows it never compiles this file at all. A defect that leaves the edge blocks outside every guarded range is therefore caught at run time on Windows alone — by this example — and on every host by the unit claims named next, which read the records by block and the produced image's scope table.
